is_anopheles.evidence: Studies field populations of Anopheles arabiensis from Tanzania (page 1, 2).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Reports testing for Vgsc L1014F (West African kdr, L995F) and L1014S (East African kdr, L995S) (page 1, 2, Table 1).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 5: 'All 978 individuals from susceptibility tests and experimental huts in Mabogini tested homozygous for the wildtype susceptible (104L) genotype. However, the SSOP-ELISA detected two out of 642 individuals from Msitu wa Tembo village that were heterozygous for the L104F kdr genotype (allele frequency = 0.16%).'

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes collected from field sites in lower Moshi, northeast Tanzania (Mabogini and Msitu wa Tembo) (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary research study reporting original field collections, assay development, and genotyping (page 1-3).

sub_country_location.evidence: Mabogini (3°22' S, 37°19' E) and Msitu wa Tembo (3°33' S, 37°17' E) in lower Moshi, Tanzania (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections occurred in 2004 (June/July 2004 in Mabogini; 2004 in Msitu wa Tembo) (page 2).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Standard primary study reporting original collections from 2004.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and collection data are reported in the main text.

assessment.summary: Development and validation of an SSOP-ELISA method to detect Vgsc L1014F and L1014S mutations, applied to 1,620 field-collected Anopheles arabiensis from Mabogini (n=978) and Msitu wa Tembo (n=642) in northern Tanzania collected in 2004. Two heterozygous L1014F individuals were detected in Msitu wa Tembo.
